**My reasoning:**

I've been farming this land in Quzhou for over 40 years. My father farmed it before me. Around here, everyone grows winter wheat then summer corn — two crops a year on the same fields. That's what I'll do again this year.

My son went to work in Shijiazhuang ten years ago, so it's mostly me and my wife now. I've been farming about 8 mu. My back isn't what it was, so I'll hire the village machinery cooperative to handle the rotary tillage and combine harvest — I pay them per mu, it's worth it.

For wheat seeds I'll buy "Jimai 22" again from the township supply store. It's a reliable variety, good disease resistance, the agronomist at the village station recommends it. For corn I'll use "Zhengdan 958" hybrid — everyone here uses it, the yields are steady. I'm not going to try something new at my age. New varieties fail and you lose the whole season.

For fertilizer, I apply compound fertilizer as base, then urea as top-dress at jointing for wheat and when corn is knee-high. I probably put on more fertilizer than I strictly need — I'd rather spend the money than risk a thin harvest when prices are decent.

Water is the main worry. The county has been pushing us to irrigate less because the groundwater is dropping. I'll cut one irrigation on the corn if the summer rains are decent, but I won't risk the wheat — wheat needs the pre-winter and jointing water no matter what.

I'll spray herbicide twice on the wheat in early spring, then fungicide in April when the weather turns wet. Corn gets one herbicide pass after emergence and one spray if I see corn borer damage.

I farm 8 mu with hired machinery for tillage and harvest. I choose proven improved wheat varieties and hybrid corn seed from the local supply store rather than experimenting with new releases. Fertilizer inputs are moderately heavy by design — I am risk-averse and prioritize yield stability over input savings. I irrigate wheat four times including the critical pre-winter and jointing waterings, and allow myself to reduce corn irrigation to two if summer rainfall cooperates. Pest and weed control follows the conventional schedule used by my neighbors: three applications on wheat and two on corn.
